_comment: QWEN3-CODER TIER-0 (2:1:1 fan-out) — the coder-specialist arm. Identical in shape to config.go-specialist-211.json so the comparison is like-for-like; the ONLY change is tier 0's model, Llama 4 Maverick 17B -> Qwen3 Coder 30B A3B. Two reasons this is the sharpest available cheap-tier test. (1) It is CHEAPER, not just better: verified us-west-2 on-demand rates are $0.15/MTok in, $0.60/MTok out against Maverick's $0.12/$0.97, and a measured 4-problem probe put a real coder sample at $0.000092 vs Maverick's profiled $0.000174 — 1.9x cheaper per sample. So a win cannot be explained away as 'we spent more', which is what confounded every prior accuracy lever (experiments 15/16/18 all bought accuracy with money and lost on cost). (2) It is purpose-built for code, where every prior cheap tier was a general instruct model. Rates are the REAL ones from the AWS Pricing API filtered to regionCode=us-west-2 (the API returns per-1K figures; these are per-MTok). Mid/large keep Claude at the same illustrative list prices every prior run used, so cross-run cost comparison holds. test_model=sonnet-4-6 differs from every tier (invariant #3). NOTE the model id is bare (qwen.*), not a us.* inference profile — `go-cascade models` calls ListInferenceProfiles and will NOT list it; it works through plain bedrock-runtime Converse, verified live, so no provider change is needed. WHAT THIS ARM CANNOT DO: at 2:1:1 tier 0's Wilson unanimous ceiling is 0.4249 (n=2), so under tau=[1,1] tier 0 can never accept no matter how good the model is — invariant #9 caps the routing score by FAN-OUT, not by accuracy. Read this arm as a test of escalation rate and mean cost/query, not of certifiable alpha. Pair it with the 5:2:1 fan-out if the acceptance question is the target.
